front_blocks.md: Define **interpreter**.

back_blocks.md: An interpreter is a type of translator that **executes high-level code line by line**.

cards.front_md: Define **interpreter**.
cards.back_md: An interpreter is a type of translator that **executes high-level code line by line**.

front_blocks.md: Does an interpreter produce a machine code file?

back_blocks.md: **No.** It does **not generate a standalone executable or machine code file**. Only immediate execution happens.

cards.front_md: Does an interpreter produce a machine code file?
cards.back_md: **No.** It does **not generate a standalone executable or machine code file**. Only immediate execution happens.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
An interpreter produces a standalone executable file.

front_blocks.md: How does an interpreter process source code?

back_blocks.md: The source code is **read, analysed and executed one line at a time**.

cards.front_md: How does an interpreter process source code?
cards.back_md: The source code is **read, analysed and executed one line at a time**.

front_blocks.md: What happens when an interpreter finds an error in a line?

back_blocks.md: **Execution stops**, and the **error is reported immediately**.

cards.front_md: What happens when an interpreter finds an error in a line?
cards.back_md: **Execution stops**, and the **error is reported immediately**.

front_blocks.md: Why is interpreted execution slower?

back_blocks.md: Each line is **translated every time** the program runs.

cards.front_md: Why is interpreted execution slower?
cards.back_md: Each line is **translated every time** the program runs.

front_blocks.md: Why is an interpreter useful during development?

back_blocks.md: It is good for **testing and debugging** while coding.

cards.front_md: Why is an interpreter useful during development?
cards.back_md: It is good for **testing and debugging** while coding.

front_blocks.md: Give two example uses of an interpreter.

back_blocks.md: **Educational tools**, such as Python shells or BASIC interpreters, and **rapid prototyping** where frequent changes are made.

front_blocks.md: Define **compilation**.

back_blocks.md: Compilation is a process that **translates a program written in a high-level programming language into machine code**.

cards.front_md: Define **compilation**.
cards.back_md: Compilation is a process that **translates a program written in a high-level programming language into machine code**.

front_blocks.md: Why is compilation necessary?

back_blocks.md: Because **only machine code can be executed by a computer**.

cards.front_md: Why is compilation necessary?
cards.back_md: Because **only machine code can be executed by a computer**.

back_blocks.md: **Lexical analysis**, **syntax analysis**, **code generation** and **optimisation**.

cards.front_md: Name the four stages of compilation.
cards.back_md: **Lexical analysis**, **syntax analysis**, **code generation** and **optimisation**.

back_blocks.md: It **identifies lexical 'tokens'** in the code, studying the **words or vocabulary** of the language.

cards.front_md: What does lexical analysis do?

front_blocks.md: Name the four types of token.

back_blocks.md: **Keywords**, **identifiers**, **operators** and **separators**.

cards.front_md: Name the four types of token.
cards.back_md: **Keywords**, **identifiers**, **operators** and **separators**.

front_blocks.md: Give two examples of a keyword token.

back_blocks.md: `var`, `const`, `function`, `for`, `while` and `if`.

cards.front_md: Give two examples of a keyword token.
cards.back_md: `var`, `const`, `function`, `for`, `while` and `if`.

front_blocks.md: What is the result of lexical analysis?

back_blocks.md: A **token table**.

front_blocks.md: What does syntax analysis do?

back_blocks.md: It makes sure the tokens all **adhere to the syntax rules** of the programming language.

cards.back_md: It makes sure the tokens all **adhere to the syntax rules** of the programming language.

front_blocks.md: Define **Abstract Syntax Tree (AST)**.

back_blocks.md: An AST is a **graph-based representation of the code being compiled**, created once the code has passed syntax analysis.

front_blocks.md: Why is an AST useful?

back_blocks.md: It is an **efficient way to represent the code** for the next stage of compilation.

cards.front_md: Why is an AST useful?
cards.back_md: It is an **efficient way to represent the code** for the next stage of compilation.

front_blocks.md: What happens at the code generation stage?

back_blocks.md: It **takes the AST and traverses it** to generate **object code** that can be executed by the computer.

cards.front_md: What happens at the code generation stage?
cards.back_md: It **takes the AST and traverses it** to generate **object code** that can be executed by the computer.

front_blocks.md: What does the optimisation stage do?

back_blocks.md: It **modifies the code to make it more efficient without changing its functionality**.

cards.front_md: What does the optimisation stage do?
cards.back_md: It **modifies the code to make it more efficient without changing its functionality**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Optimisation makes the code more efficient **without changing its functionality**.

**False.**

front_blocks.md: Give a common optimisation action.

back_blocks.md: **Removing duplicate code**. If an 'add' function is written twice in the source code, a sophisticated compiler includes it only once in the object code.

cards.front_md: Give a common optimisation action.
cards.back_md: **Removing duplicate code**. If an 'add' function is written twice in the source code, a sophisticated compiler includes it only once in the object code.

front_blocks.md: Define **syntax**.

back_blocks.md: Syntax is the set of **strict rules that define how code must be written**.

cards.front_md: Define **syntax**.
cards.back_md: Syntax is the set of **strict rules that define how code must be written**.

front_blocks.md: Do all programming languages share the same syntax?

back_blocks.md: **No.** Each language has its own syntax. For example, Python uses indentation and Java uses semicolons.

cards.front_md: Do all programming languages share the same syntax?
cards.back_md: **No.** Each language has its own syntax. For example, Python uses indentation and Java uses semicolons.

front_blocks.md: Why must syntax be precisely defined?

back_blocks.md: To **avoid ambiguity**, so that translators can correctly convert the program into a form the CPU can understand.

cards.front_md: Why must syntax be precisely defined?
cards.back_md: To **avoid ambiguity**, so that translators can correctly convert the program into a form the CPU can understand.

back_blocks.md: To **describe simple patterns** in text or syntax, such as variable names or simple statements.

front_blocks.md: Define **Backus-Naur Form (BNF)**.

back_blocks.md: BNF is a **meta-language**, a way of writing rules that define the **syntax of programming languages or data structures**.

front_blocks.md: Name three things BNF is used for.

back_blocks.md: To describe **formal grammar**, to define how statements and expressions are **structured**, and to ensure syntax rules are **unambiguous and machine-readable**.

cards.front_md: Name three things BNF is used for.

back_blocks.md: **No need for brackets**, **easier for computers to evaluate using a stack**, and it is always **unambiguous**.

front_blocks.md: What determines the order of operations in RPN?

back_blocks.md: **Position**, not parentheses.

cards.front_md: What determines the order of operations in RPN?
cards.back_md: **Position**, not parentheses.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
RPN needs brackets to show precedence.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
RPN follows the evaluation order naturally, so there is **no need for brackets** or precedence rules.

front_blocks.md: Which data structure is used to evaluate RPN?

back_blocks.md: A **stack**.

cards.front_md: Which data structure is used to evaluate RPN?
cards.back_md: A **stack**.

front_blocks.md: What are the four steps of evaluating an RPN expression?

back_blocks.md: **Read left to right**; **push numbers onto the stack**; when an **operator** is read, **pop the top two values**, **apply the operator** and **push the result back**; when the expression ends, the result is at the **top of the stack**.

cards.front_md: What are the four steps of evaluating an RPN expression?
cards.back_md: **Read left to right**; **push numbers onto the stack**; when an **operator** is read, **pop the top two values**, **apply the operator** and **push the result back**; when the expression ends, the result is at the **top of the stack**.

front_blocks.md: What happens when an operator is read?

back_blocks.md: The **top two values are popped** from the stack, the **operator is applied**, and the **result is pushed back** onto the stack.

cards.front_md: What happens when an operator is read?
cards.back_md: The **top two values are popped** from the stack, the **operator is applied**, and the **result is pushed back** onto the stack.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
In RPN, an operator is applied to the bottom two values of the stack.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
It is applied to the **top two values**, which are popped from the stack.

**True or False?**

In RPN, an operator is applied to the bottom two values of the stack.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

It is applied to the **top two values**, which are popped from the stack.

front_blocks.md: Where is the final result of an RPN evaluation found?

back_blocks.md: At the **top of the stack**.

cards.front_md: Where is the final result of an RPN evaluation found?
cards.back_md: At the **top of the stack**.
